title: Flutter 3.38.1: Failed to Verify when Submitting to App Store Connect
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Validating the archive gives the following messages:

```err
Validation failed
The binary is invalid. The encryption info in the LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO load command is either missing or invalid, or the binary is already encrypted. This binary does not seem to have been built with Apple's linker. (ID: .....)
```

### Expected results

No errors before upgrading to Flutter 3.38.1


### Flutter Doctor output

<details open><summary>Doctor output</summary>

```console
Doctor summary (to see all details, run flutter doctor -v):
[✓] Flutter (Channel stable, 3.38.1, on macOS 15.6.1 24G90 darwin-arm64, locale en-US)
[✓] Android toolchain - develop for Android devices (Android SDK version 36.0.0)
[✓] Xcode - develop for iOS and macOS (Xcode 16.3)
```

</details>

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: Okay I was able to reproduce your issue. It seems sometimes `sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework` is created and embedded in the app and sometimes it isn't. When it is, it will cause validation to fail: Steps where `sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework` is created: 1. `flutter clean` 2. `flutter build ios --config-only` 3. Build targeting a simulator in Xcode or do `flutter build ios --simulator` 4. Archive through Xcode 5. Validate will fail due to `sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework` Steps where `sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework` is not created: 1. `flutter clean` 2. `flutter build ios --config-only` 3. Archive through Xcode 4. Validate will pass because `sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework` is not included in the app bundle It appears that once `sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework` is generated, it is always embedded in the app (even if you're not targeting a simulator), which is likely a mistake. I recommend you file an issue with the plugin. This is not a Flutter issue so I'm closing.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Thanks for sharing these reproduction steps 👍 

> This is not a Flutter issue

Are you sure? Flutter is the tool creating those frameworks based on code assets emitted by hooks, I believe this happens [here](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/882c29a1947c183943394b67de5950750e03fbe6/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/isolated/native_assets/ios/native_assets.dart#L95-L137).

So this:

> It appears that once `sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework` is generated, it is always embedded in the app (even if you're not targeting a simulator), which is likely a mistake.

sounds like a Flutter bug to me.

The `sqlite3` package is not a Flutter plugin and can't add frameworks to the build directly.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
It took me a while to find this poking through all the different steps involving native assets, but the root cause is most likely this:

1. The actual native assets builders (as in, code in `lib/src/isolated/native_assets/`) behave correctly. They don't mess up the build and emit assets they need into `build/native_assets/ios/sqlite3arm64ios.framework` and `build/native_assets/ios/sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework`. They also emit a file into `flutter_assets/NativeAssetsManifest.json` that correctly describes which native assets the app needs.
3. However, [this method](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/2b5fa9462ce9599152ae3c7cc1a0b8b5c63eed0c/packages/flutter_tools/bin/xcode_backend.dart#L341-L342) which gets invoked as part of an iOS build then copies the entire `build/native_assets/ios` directory into `build/ios/Release-iphoneos/Runner.app/Frameworks/`, which is incorrect because the source folder might contain assets that aren't actually needed by the particular target.
It looks like having a single `build/native_assets/ios` directory (as opposed to `ios/` and `ios-sim/`) [was intentional](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/2b5fa9462ce9599152ae3c7cc1a0b8b5c63eed0c/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/isolated/native_assets/native_assets.dart#L365). So I believe the correct behavior of `_embedNativeAssets` would be to read `native_assets.json` and only copy frameworks that are actually referenced in the build. ~~That would require reading the `.last_build_id` file from `build/ios/Release-iphoneos`.~~

I'm happy to open a PR for this, but it would be helpful if someone from the Flutter team could confirm whether this sounds like the right path. Especially the part about reading `.last_build_id` in the `embed` / `embed_and_thin` phase sounds a bit hacky. I can't find a better approach though.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
@participant6 What do you think about https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/178602#issuecomment-3592035151? Looks like the plugin is using dart hooks to create native assets and generate different assets [depending](https://github.com/participant5/sqlite3.dart/blob/a6ebb6eb471a49bb84e1077092e648f4a631f143/sqlite3/lib/src/hook/assets.dart#L177-L178) on if targeting a simulator or physical device. Should Flutter only embed the frameworks in the native_assets.json from the current build?

If yes, then likely we should change something in `flutter assemble` (perhaps the `DartBuild` target?) to copy the correct native assets into the `BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR` and then in [xcode_backend.dart](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/2b5fa9462ce9599152ae3c7cc1a0b8b5c63eed0c/packages/flutter_tools/bin/xcode_backend.dart#L329-L378) copy them from the `BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR` to the `TARGET_BUILD_DIR`, like we do with the Flutter framework.

comments.body:
The solution for me was to downgrade to `Flutter 3.39.0-1.0.pre-273`


Downgrading to that flutter SDK solves the LC_ENCRYPT problem, but then a new problem arises having to do with version numbers, so then I goto Xcode and make a script with the following, which solves that.  This is all pretty dumb so hopefully the core issue of LC_ENCRYPT gets solved

```
# Define the path to the App.framework Info.plist
APP_FRAMEWORK_INFO_PLIST="${BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR}/${FRAMEWORKS_FOLDER_PATH}/App.framework/Info.plist"

# !!! Get the MinimumOSVersion dynamically from Xcode build settings !!!
# This reads the setting you typically update in the General or Build Settings tab
MIN_OS_VERSION="${IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET}" 

# Check if the file exists before trying to modify it
if [ -f "$APP_FRAMEWORK_INFO_PLIST" ]; then
    echo "Updating $APP_FRAMEWORK_INFO_PLIST with MinimumOSVersion $MIN_OS_VERSION (Dynamically sourced)"
    
    # Use PlistBuddy to add or update the MinimumOSVersion key
    /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Set :MinimumOSVersion $MIN_OS_VERSION" "$APP_FRAMEWORK_INFO_PLIST" || \
    /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Add :MinimumOSVersion string $MIN_OS_VERSION" "$APP_FRAMEWORK_INFO_PLIST"
else
    echo "Warning: App.framework Info.plist not found at expected path."
fi
```

comments.author: participant25
comments.body: This issue was/is kind of blocking for me so I had to find a workaround which fixes the problem at least temporarily. I also upgraded to the latest flutter master branch (where the initial fix was merged) but it still happened. Therefore I am commenting here because maybe my workaround is helpful for someone else as well: I let codex analyze my archives (which failed to validate in Xcode) combined with the flutter source code and my app code and after nearly an hour it found the root cause: > Flutter's AOT snapshot for iOS is produced by `gen_snapshot`, which writes a Mach-O dylib (`App.framework/App`). On current Flutter master (as of 2026-01-06), that dylib was missing a valid `LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO` load command. App Store Connect rejects this because it expects a dylib linked by Apple's linker with correct load commands. It was just missing - so the obvious workaround is to add this load command manually again: 1) Open `ios/Runner.xcworkspace` in Xcode. 2) Select the **Runner** target. 3) Go to **Build Phases**. 4) Click the **+** button → **New Run Script Phase**. 5) Name it: **Relink App.framework (Apple ld)**. 6) Drag this phase so it sits **after** the Flutter **"Run Script"** phase and **before** **"Thin Binary"**. 7) Paste the following script into the phase: ```bash set -euo pipefail if [ "${CONFIGURATION}" != "Release" ]; then exit 0 fi APP_FRAMEWORK_DIR="${BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR}/App.framework" APP_BIN="${APP_FRAMEWORK_DIR}/App" APP_O=$(ls -t "${PROJECT_DIR}/../.dart_tool/flutter_build"/*/arm64/app.o 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true) if [ -z "${APP_O}" ] || [ ! -f "${APP_O}" ]; then echo "warning: app.o not found; skipping App.framework relink" exit 0 fi SDKROOT=$(xcrun --sdk iphoneos --show-sdk-path) /usr/bin/xcrun --sdk iphoneos clang -arch arm64 -dynamiclib "${APP_O}" -isysroot "${SDKROOT}" \ -Wl,-install_name,@rpath/App.framework/App \ -Wl,-rpath,@executable_path/Frameworks \ -Wl,-rpath,@loader_path/Frameworks \ -o "${APP_BIN}" chmod +x "${APP_BIN}" ``` Run `flutter build iOS` again, run the `Archive` in Xcode again and then the distribution/validation should work again (for me it finally did). You might have to modify the path to the "flutter_build" tool - this was just my setup.

Fixed on stable. [Cherry-pick to beta in progress](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/180687).
